authority.legal_name: Transtejo & Soflusa (TTSL), the State-owned Tagus ferry operator

mandate.summary: Transtejo and Soflusa are Portugal's State-owned operators of the Tagus river ferries, carrying tens of millions of passengers a year across the estuary between Lisbon and the south-bank towns, integrated with Carris Metropolitana and the Navegante card.
current_priorities: Daily cross-estuary commuting between Lisbon and the south bank
Integration with the metropolitan transport and Navegante ticketing
Fleet renewal — a fleet of new battery-electric ferries on order

policy_targets.vision: Portugal Carbon Neutrality Roadmap 2050 / Lisbon climate action
policy_targets.decarb_note: Portugal targets carbon neutrality by 2050, and Transtejo is already replacing its diesel fleet with battery-electric ferries — but the busiest corridors still need faster, higher-frequency service.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the foiling upgrade to a network the State already runs and is already electrifying — faster, higher-frequency estuary crossings that relieve the bridges while extending the same zero-emission direction the new electric ferries have set.

precedent.headline: State-run Tagus ferries are core commuter infrastructure, not a novelty.
precedent.network: Transtejo and Soflusa run year-round commuter ferries across the Tagus — Cais do Sodré–Cacilhas, –Seixal, –Montijo, the Soflusa Barreiro line and the Belém–Trafaria–Porto Brandão line — and have a fleet of new battery-electric ferries on order.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the foiling upgrade to a network the State already runs and is already electrifying — faster, higher-frequency estuary crossings that relieve the bridges while extending the same zero-emission direction the new electric ferries have set.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public stops; new/committed/study stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The busiest Tagus crossing — central Lisbon to Cacilhas in minutes.
Commuter line to the south-bank town of Seixal.
Soflusa commuter line to Barreiro and the rail interchange.
West-Lisbon crossing to Trafaria on the south bank.
Short west-Lisbon hop to Porto Brandão.
North-bank waterfront line linking central Lisbon to Belém.
South-bank link between the two western terminals.

regional_links.note: Domestic-only network across the Tagus estuary. No cross-border links in scope.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: The estuary has strong tidal currents and shifting sandbanks (e.g. off Trafaria/Cova do Vapor) — follow the marked channels and hand-waypoint around the bars.
The 25 de Abril and Vasco da Gama bridge piers sit in the fairway — waypoint clear of the pier protection zones.
Lisbon is a busy commercial and cruise port; cross the shipping channel at marked points with low-wake transit near terminals.
The south-bank estuary reserves require low-wake operation near the shore and mudflats.
